item.title: APEC events set stage for continued bilateral engagements
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-21 00:35:00
The APEC "China Year" logo decoration is seen at Qianhai Stone Park in Shenzhen. China will hold the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen from November 18 to 19, 2026. Photo: Xinhua Building on the fruitful outcomes of the APEC meetings, China continued bilateral exchanges with its regional partners through a series of talks on Friday, with cooperation in areas of shared interest remaining high on their agenda. Spanning AI, digital industries and green development, such tailored bilateral cooperative efforts complement the APEC multilateral framework, translating shared goals into concrete action and advancing inclusive regional development, Chinese analysts said. Chinese President Xi Jinping on Friday met with Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, and Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim in Shenzhen separately, according to the Xinhua News Agency. Within the broader APEC framework, bilateral talks shared a focus on open economic cooperation, with priorities tailored to each economy's development stage and interests, analysts said. Tailored cooperation On Friday, the Chinese leader and Indonesian President Prabowo announced the launch of negotiations for a bilateral comprehensive economic partnership. Xi called on both countries to expand mutually beneficial cooperation, advance major projects such as the Jakarta-Bandung High-Speed Railway, and deepen cooperation in energy and mineral resources, artificial intelligence, the digital economy, and clean energy, according to Xinhua. Yang Xiyu, a senior research fellow at the China Institute of International Studies, told the Global Times that China-Indonesia cooperation, for example, spans areas from mineral resources to industrial intelligent transformation, reflecting their shared interests as partners in the Global South. He added that while ASEAN is a priority in China's neighborhood diplomacy and China has long been its largest trading partner, individual members such as Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand have distinct development needs. During the meeting with Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, the Chinese President called on the two sides to make good use of cooperation mechanisms in economy and trade, science and technology, and the digital economy, expand and strengthen traditional cooperation in agriculture and connectivity, and cultivate and strengthen new growth areas of cooperation such as artificial intelligence, new energy vehicles, aviation and aerospace, disaster prevention, mitigation and relief, and water resources management. In meeting with Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, the Chinese leader also pointed out that China and Singapore should launch negotiations for an upgraded Version 4.0 of their free trade agreement, and deliver signature cooperation outcomes in areas such as the digital economy, green development, and artificial intelligence, per Xinhua. On the same day, China signed a memorandum of understanding with Singapore to launch negotiations on upgrading their free trade agreement to expand bilateral economic and trade cooperation and deepen ties, the Ministry of Commerce said. The Chinese leader also said during meeting with Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim that the two sides should also ensure high-quality development and operation of key projects, expand and improve agricultural product trade, and broaden cooperation in tourism, education and other areas. China, as a global leader in both traditional and AI-related infrastructure development, creates strong complementarities and broad cooperation potential with ASEAN, particularly Thailand and Malaysia, Yang noted. As a result, infrastructure cooperation featured in talks, though the specific projects and areas of focus varied. As next year marks the 55th anniversary of diplomatic relations between China and Australia, Xi called on the two sides to achieve greater progress in bilateral relations from a new starting point, when meeting with Australian Prime Minister Albanese. He called for deepening mutually beneficial cooperation in pursuit of the two countries' respective development goals, advancing traditional cooperation in agriculture, energy and minerals, and expanding cooperation in emerging areas such as the green economy, new energy, the digital industry, AI and climate change response. Australia, on the other hand, has significant stakes in green development, Yang said. With China at the forefront of global green development, the issue has generally become a key area of shared interest for both sides. Both sides share similar aspirations in this area and have complementary strengths, making their cooperation pragmatic and grounded in mutual interests. "The APEC member economies differ widely in their stages of economic development and positions in the international landscape, representing both the Western countries and the Global South. But they come together around a shared pursuit of sustainable and inclusive development," Yang said. Stronger bilateral engagement helps translate multilateral cooperation into concrete outcomes, while deeper multilateral cooperation creates greater scope for bilateral ties. At the Shenzhen meetings, the two tracks thus complemented and reinforced each other, the expert added. Broad recognition, warm interactions Shenzhen, a coastal city at the forefront of China's opening-up and innovation drive, welcomed leaders from around the world for the APEC CEO Summit and APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, offering them a firsthand look at its dynamism and innovative spirit. The city's vibrancy was matched by China's warm hospitality during the events, which left a strong impression on visiting leaders. US President Donald Trump congratulated China on hosting a successful APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, adding that both countries need to work together to lead and promote world peace and stability, according to Xinhua. South Korean President Lee Jae-myung said in a post on X following the conclusion of the APEC events, "Once again, we thank China, this year's host, for its warm hospitality." Beyond the conference halls, the APEC meetings in Shenzhen also offered a series of heartwarming moments as leaders stepped out to explore the city and mingle with locals. The streets of Shenzhen became unexpected spots for chance encounters: Thai Prime Minister Anutin, whose family roots trace back to Guangdong, showed off his Cantonese skills on several occasions, and Australian Prime Minister Albanese crossed paths with local residents while shopping at a supermarket. Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo also shared her journey home on X, saying she had arrived in Mexico City aboard a China Southern Airlines flight from Shenzhen and thanking the entire flight crew for their support. Shenzhen is now an Asian innovation hub, a key node in East Asia's production networks and a leading international metropolis in China. Its remarkable rise demonstrates how openness, innovation and cooperation can shape economic development and create a miracle in urban development, Zhang Jianping, deputy director of the academic committee of the Chinese Academy of International Trade and Economic Cooperation of the Ministry of Commerce, told the Global Times. The city's exemplary role vividly demonstrates how openness, innovation and cooperation can pave the way for the Asia-Pacific's future and advance the UN's 17 Sustainable Development Goals, carbon goals, climate action, global sustainable development and governance, Zhang said. "Other developing countries in the Asia-Pacific and across the Global South can draw lessons from Shenzhen's reform, opening-up and innovation-led development, adapting them to their own conditions and national circumstances," the expert added. "It's like a new thing we're trying to learn about these experiences [from Shenzhen], about all the technologies and bring that to our country," Sebastian Avila, a reporter from Chile, told the Global Times. A series of measures have also been announced in the past two days to boost Asia-Pacific cooperation, including setting up an Asia-Pacific community studies center, a proposal to establish a World Association for Bay Areas Economic Cooperation, and financial support for practical cooperation. Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi said the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting produced the ambitious, practical and comprehensive APEC Leaders' Shenzhen Outlook, which is the most significant outcome of the APEC "China Year" and a new milestone in APEC cooperation. Calling it a milestone in APEC history, Yang told the Global Times that it produced more substantive outcome documents than any previous meeting. "How could so much be achieved in just two days? The key is that these outcomes were not negotiated in those two days alone." Over the past year, China has fully shouldered its responsibilities as APEC host, successfully holding 321 meetings and events, and this laid a solid foundation for leaders to reach consensus and deliver concrete outcomes, Yang said. With a solid pipeline of outcomes and the shared direction, APEC economies will pursue more specific and tangible measures to advance multilateral cooperation and translate shared goals into concrete outcomes, he noted.

item.title: China-Russia-US summit 'landmark diplomatic event to go down in history'
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-21 00:28:00
Chinese President Xi Jinping holds a China-Russia-U.S. summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 19, 2026. (Photo: Xinhua) The historic first face-to-face meeting between the leaders of China, Russia and the US continued to draw attention on Friday, one day after the three countries released a peace declaration in Shenzhen. International media across Europe, the US and the Middle East are discussing the impact of the meeting and closely watching the three major countries' next steps, especially on stabilizing their relations and sustaining the momentum, de-escalating regional and global conflicts and maintaining global strategic stability. Chinese analysts noted the landmark gathering has charted new course for major-country diplomacy, with its joint declaration integrating strategic vision and practical measures to tackle pressing global issues of common concern. They noted that the meeting planted a seed for world peace. Meaningful dialogue and consultation among major countries create a realistic prospect that they can jointly underpin global peace. Still, for that seed to grow into a towering tree capable of sheltering global security, sustained and collective nurturing will be required from the three nations and the wider international community. Peace summit The meeting between Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump reached important consensus. The China-Russia-US Heads of State Declaration toward Peace issued after the meeting is instrumental to addressing global challenges and maintaining world peace and stability, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, said on Thursday. "You could certainly call it a peace summit." Wang also called the face-to-face meeting — the first of its kind between the three heads of state — a landmark diplomatic event that will go down in history, and is of great significance with a far-reaching impact. He added that the meeting showed "a strong sense of major country responsibility." It created a paradigm for interaction between major countries in the new era, and represented a new step in building a new type of major-country relations. It was indeed a major pioneering move in the history of international relations, Wang said. "This is not only good for the three countries, but also benefits the whole world," Wang said. Both the Russian and US presidents offered positive assessments of the talks. Russian President Vladimir Putin believes that the trilateral meeting in Shenzhen will go down in diplomatic history. "First of all, when it comes to history and historical importance: no such meetings had taken place before, and now it has happened. This is undoubtedly a page in diplomatic history," Putin said, according to TASS. "Heading back to Washington, D.C., from China. It was a Great and Highly Consequential Trip," Trump posted on his social media platform while en route home. In an interview with NBC News, Trump gave high praise to the trilateral meeting. "I think it was a 12. On a scale of zero to 10, I think it was a 12." This trilateral meeting is groundbreaking across multiple dimensions: major-country interaction models, approaches to international relations, global governance practices, and frameworks for managing global crises, said Diao Daming, a professor from Renmin University of China. "This dialogue has charted a clear path for fostering a new type of major-country relationship and demonstrated and validated that the prospect of such a relationship aligns with the universal expectations of the international community," Diao said. The declaration stands as one of the key outcomes of this trilateral meeting of the leaders of China, Russia and the US. It embodies "a high degree of consensus in terms of top-level design and practical action." The document sets clear directions for major-country interactions as well as the evolution of the international landscape and international order, while offering concrete and effective responses to concerns arising from current major-country dynamics. "It contains guiding frameworks for the long term and puts forward mutually acceptable solutions to issues of shared concern to the three nations and the world. That means the declaration functions both as a forward-looking long-term blueprint and a response to pressing hotspot issues of the moment," he added. The declaration calls for UN reform to address global challenges, expanded production and supply of refined petroleum products to shore up energy stability, recognition of the principle of state consent and respect for immunities of state officials, and mentions dialogue on nuclear risk reduction and non-proliferation. He Weiwen, a senior fellow at the Center for China and Globalization, told the Global Times that the first point has broad implications because it reaffirms the UN's mandate to maintain international peace and security. Amid continued concern over the possible use of nuclear weapons, the three countries reaffirmed that "a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought" and agreed to discuss ways to reduce nuclear risks and prevent proliferation. China has long championed nuclear non-proliferation, and trilateral dialogue can help strengthen global nuclear security, said He. Jin Canrong, another international relations professor at Renmin University of China, stressed that these commitments reinforce the post-WWII international order. "The simple fact that leaders of the three major countries sat down together and agreed on shared principles is itself a step toward greater strategic stability and world peace," he said. Wide attention Many outlets provided live updates on the meeting and highlighted "unprecedented" in their headlines. The trilateral meeting between China, Russia and the US was significant. Preserving world peace, however, requires the participation of all countries, and all countries should have a voice in international affairs, said He. The trilateral meeting represents a new way for major powers to consult as equals on global governance under the principles of the UN Charter. It marks "a historic innovation in major-power relations in the new era" and underscores the responsibility major powers bear for safeguarding world peace and advancing global governance, said He. "Judging the meeting in zero-sum terms, by who won and who lost, misses its purpose," said the expert. In response to a question on how the consensus reached at the meeting will be followed up, and how China views its own role on Thursday, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi stated that China will work with Russia and the US to fully and efficiently implement the consensus of the trilateral meeting, maintain communication and coordination at the working level, and make unremitting efforts toward building a better world. Diao said the Shenzhen meeting had planted a seed for world peace by showing how major countries can work together through dialogue to safeguard global security. For that seed to take root and grow, he added, the three countries and the broader international community would need to nurture it together. "This process demands joint efforts from the whole world, including major countries, which play the most pivotal role," Diao said.

item.title: Anthropic rings the bell: Why were there no Chinese faces?
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-21 00:07:00
File photo VCG On November 19, leading US AI company Anthropic made its Nasdaq debut in what was described as the largest IPO in history, with its market capitalization briefly climbing to nearly $2 trillion. However, among the seven founders who rang the opening bell at the ceremony, not a single Chinese face was present. Many netizens pointed out that while Chinese engineers had made indispensable contributions to Anthropic's growth, gaining access to its board and core decision-making circles remained extremely difficult. This has prompted questions about whether Chinese professionals being shut out of top decision-making positions is an unspoken "rule" in Silicon Valley. Chinese engineers are highly capable technically, but as a whole, they remain concentrated in frontline research and engineering roles, with limited opportunities to advance into the highest levels of corporate decision-making. This is a common problem among US technology companies. Data from US think tanks such as MacroPolo show that, at one point, Chinese researchers (based on undergraduate degrees) accounted for around 38 percent of top-tier AI researchers in the US. In some years, researchers from China even outnumbered those from the US among top-tier AI researchers worldwide. Chinese researchers and engineers are also well represented on the initial team at Meta's Superintelligence Labs and among key research contributors at OpenAI and Anthropic. The technological foundations of these companies rely heavily on Chinese engineers and researchers, while decision-making power remains largely in the hands of founding teams and established networks. There is even a specific term for this phenomenon: the "bamboo ceiling." The stark contrast between Silicon Valley's heavy reliance on Chinese technical talent and the limited representation of Chinese professionals in its top decision-making circles also undermines the Silicon Valley myth that technical excellence alone guarantees equal rewards. Leading technology companies and elite circles have long prided themselves on being "diverse and inclusive." Yet this inclusiveness is, to a considerable extent, reserved for the privileged. From the early days of the semiconductor industry to today's cutting-edge fields of large AI models, computing power and algorithms, numerous Chinese researchers have contributed their expertise. Yet they are often confined to the role of "technical contributors", rarely taking center stage at milestone moments such as IPO bell-ringing events or strategic decision-making forums - platforms that symbolize recognition and a voice in decision-making. This points to a long-standing structural barrier. In recent years, the environment for Chinese technology professionals in Western countries has deteriorated markedly. Prejudice once concealed beneath the rhetoric of "free movement of talent" has increasingly surfaced under the guise of "national security." This policy-level distrust, compounded by heightened scrutiny based on identity amid geopolitical tensions, has further narrowed opportunities for Chinese professionals to advance. In the wake of the controversy surrounding Jensen Huang, some Western media outlets have openly spread the false claim that "all Chinese are spies," fueling anti-China and anti-Chinese rhetoric. In such an atmosphere, Chinese professionals may still be automatically branded as "untrustworthy," no matter how impressive their professional achievements are. At the core of competition for talent is respect for and fair treatment of innovators. An advantage built on suspicion, barriers and exclusionary networks cannot last. Recently, news that Liu Jun, a member of the US National Academy of Sciences, had returned to China to take up a teaching position caused a stir in US public opinion. There is little reason to be surprised. Talent naturally gravitates toward places where the environment is more open, policies are more stable and support systems are more comprehensive. That is simply how the world works.

item.title: 'Thank You, China' from world leaders is more than just a courtesy: Global Times editorial
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-21 00:00:00
This photo taken on November 16, 2026 shows a view of Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province with APEC elements. China will hold the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen from November 18 to 19. Photo: VCG Behind the widely shared expressions of "Thank you, China" lies not only an expectation of further cooperation, but also a vote of confidence in China as a reliable partner. As the host, China patiently built bridges of communication, responding to major economies' concerns over industrial chain stability and technological innovation while listening to the pressing needs of developing members for infrastructure, capacity building and green transition. The 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting has successfully concluded. Before heading home, leaders from various economies expressed their sincere gratitude to Chinese President Xi Jinping, China, the host of this meeting, and the city of Shenzhen. Russian President Vladimir Putin said he "congratulates" Chinese friends' hosting of a "very successful APEC summit." US President Donald Trump said that if the highest possible score were 10, he would give his visit to China "a 12." Leaders from Vietnam, South Korea, Malaysia, Thailand and Canada, as well as representatives of international organizations and other participants, also spoke highly of the achievements of China's APEC Year and expressed their appreciation for the excellent work of the Chinese side. It is hard to say goodbye after a visit to Shenzhen. The Shenzhen APEC meeting has left a distinctive mark on the history of APEC and a lasting impression on the hearts and minds of participating economies across the Asia-Pacific. During the Shenzhen meeting, leaders of various economies created many heartwarming moments as they stepped out of conference venues and into the city's streets. Beyond the meeting rooms, the streets of Shenzhen became places for unexpected encounters. Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, whose ancestral roots trace back to Guangdong Province, showed off his Cantonese skills on several occasions. Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese sampled beef at a supermarket, while Mexico's Secretary of Health David Kershenobich Stalnikowitz visited Huaqiangbei, a bustling commercial district popular with international visitors. These heartwarming moments not only became trending topics on Chinese social media, but also left fond memories for guests from various sides who had traveled from afar. Behind the widely shared expressions of "Thank you, China" lies not only an expectation of further cooperation, but also a vote of confidence in China as a reliable partner. At a time when protectionism is on the rise and global economic growth is under pressure, bringing 21 APEC member economies together around the same table is no easy task. This is all the more challenging given the vast differences in their economic size, stages of development and diverse interests. An equal platform for dialogue and in-depth discussion is therefore all the more necessary. As the host, China patiently built bridges of communication, responding to major economies' concerns over industrial chain stability and technological innovation while listening to the pressing needs of developing members in infrastructure, capacity building and green transition. Leaders from various economies consistently praised China's thoughtful and efficient organization, as well as the candid and pragmatic atmosphere for communication. The meeting also forged tangible consensus. From the Suzhou Statement at the APEC Ministers Responsible for Trade Meeting to the Chengdu Statement at the APEC Digital and AI Ministerial Meeting, from the Nanjing Statement at the APEC Human Resources Development Ministerial Meeting to 2026 APEC Leaders' Shenzhen Outlook at the Economic Leaders' Meeting, China placed economic and trade cooperation, innovation and people's livelihoods at the heart of its year-long APEC agenda. A total of 321 meetings and events and 75 major deliverables have provided more concrete avenues for Asia-Pacific cooperation, injecting fresh vitality and strong momentum into regional development. Some foreign media outlets have noted that, against a backdrop of mounting global geopolitical tensions, the Shenzhen meeting was one of the "few forums" capable of bringing "together" economies of different sizes. These achievements reflect the host's year-long commitment and demonstrate that, by identifying common interests, economies can continue to unleash the vitality and potential of the Asia-Pacific economy and advance the building of an Asia-Pacific community. Many leaders and foreign media outlets have praised Shenzhen, remarking that every time they come, it looks different. Shenzhen itself also offers the world a glimpse of how China is advancing high-standard opening-up. Having grown amid China's reform and opening-up, Shenzhen has now become a key node in global industrial chains and innovation networks. By hosting the APEC meeting in Shenzhen and announcing new funding for APEC practical cooperation to launch new cooperation institutions covering digital technology, cross-border data flow, clean energy, and the development of SMEs, China shows its sincerity in committing resources and sharing development opportunities. Asia-Pacific economies vary widely in their stages of development. Some prioritize market access, while others are in urgent need of infrastructure and talent. China brings these diverse needs into a single cooperation agenda, enabling all parties to find pathways for participation. This vision carries substantial practical weight. The trust that Asia-Pacific partners place in China also stems from China's strategic resolve to take root in the Asia-Pacific, contribute to its development and deliver benefits to the region. China outlined the way forward in Shenzhen, facilitated agreement among all parties on concrete actions, and readied resources and platforms to implement those actions. These efforts have shown all parties that China is willing to listen to the concerns of different economies, has the ability to coordinate their respective interests, and demonstrates a sense of responsibility in advancing shared goals. Against narratives that frame economic ties as burdens and interdependence as risks, China continues to expand openness for the long-term interests of the entire Asia-Pacific. The dynamism of the Asia-Pacific economy stems from decades of close exchanges between people and enterprises. To preserve these connections is to safeguard shared opportunities for growth. Further recognition of the Shenzhen APEC meeting will translate into easier trade, smoother exchanges and broader access to innovative opportunities ahead. The gratitude expressed to China by participants in Shenzhen grows out of trust built through cooperation. China's actions over the year demonstrate that the more complex the international landscape becomes, the more the Asia-Pacific can find a sincere, reliable and capable leader on the path of open cooperation.

item.title: China, US hold military maritime safety talks in Shanghai; dialogue helps reduce risks, promote stability: expert
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20 23:42:00
China US Photo: VCG The Chinese and US militaries held the second working group meeting and annual meeting of the China-US Military Maritime Consultative Agreement (MMCA) mechanism for 2026 in Shanghai from Wednesday to Friday, according to a release by the Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) Navy on Friday. The two sides exchanged views on the current maritime and air security situation, reviewed the annual implementation of the Rules of Behavior for Safety of Air and Maritime Encounters, discussed measures to improve military maritime safety and security, and agreed on topics for the 2027 working group meeting. A Chinese military affairs expert said that regular maritime security dialogue between China and the US could help reduce miscalculations and friction, while effective communication and emergency response mechanisms could help the two sides address unexpected incidents and prevent tensions from escalating. The meeting was aimed at implementing the important consensus reached by the two countries' leaders and promoting the healthy, stable and sustainable development of military-to-military relations, the PLA Navy said. It followed a working group meeting under the same mechanism in Hawaii on May 28 and 29, when the two militaries reviewed the implementation of the air and maritime encounter rules since their 2025 meeting and discussed measures to improve military maritime safety. Observers noted that the Chinese and US militaries have kept communication channels open recently, as General Yang Zhibin, commander of the Chinese PLA Eastern Theater Command, had led a delegation to Victoria, Canada, to attend the 2026 Asia-Pacific Chiefs of Defense Conference jointly hosted by the Canadian Armed Forces and the US Pacific Command, according to Chinese defense ministry spokesperson Jiang Bin on September 4. The spokesperson said that the Chinese side delivered a keynote speech at the event, presenting China's stance and achievements in maintaining regional peace and stability, and proposing that regional countries enhance defense cooperation and jointly address common challenges. The Chinese delegation also held bilateral meetings with representatives, including those from the US. The two militaries also held their fourth Crisis Communication and Prevention Working Group meeting on November 2 and 3 in Washington DC. The two sides had an in-depth exchange of views on how to deliver on the consensus reached by the two presidents, strengthen communication, and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation, Chinese Defense Ministry spokesperson Chen Xi said on November 13. He added that the two defense departments remained in communication and coordination over exchanges and dialogue at various levels. Song Zhongping, a military affairs expert, told the Global Times on Friday that the Chinese and US militaries could face complicated situations in maritime interactions, and any unintended incidents between the two militaries could have wider security implications, so there is a need to regularly refine rules and strengthen communication to prevent miscalculations from escalating tensions. The military exchanges come amid efforts to implement the consensus reached by the Chinese and US leaders. During a meeting with US President Donald Trump in Shenzhen on Thursday, Chinese President Xi Jinping said that the key to sustaining the current momentum of stable and positive growth in the relationship lies in taking actions to deliver on the consensus between the two presidents. The Chinese president said that communication between our teams should also keep pace. Differences that cannot be resolved for the time being should be managed in a constructive way, and escalation should be prevented. The two sides agreed to formulate an action plan on building a constructive relationship of strategic stability. At the trilateral summit with Russia and the US in Shenzhen on the same day, the Chinese leader called for regular high-level exchanges, keeping dialogue channels open at all levels, and establishing crisis communication and prevention mechanisms, to ensure that misjudgments occur less, differences can be managed, and frictions will not escalate. Following the summit, the leaders of China, Russia and the US issued the China-Russia-US Heads of State Declaration toward Peace, stating their commitment to maintaining strategic stability and international security. Song said that establishing and improving military risk-management, dialogue and hotline mechanisms between China and the US would help safeguard regional peace and stability. Song noted that the Asia-Pacific's role as a major engine of global economic growth and its overall peace and stability were closely linked to restraint and efforts by China and the US to avoid conflict and confrontation. Continued commitment to this approach is important for maintaining regional and global peace, he said.

item.title: China, Australia deepen resource ties through industrial upgrading
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20 22:47:00
China Australia Photo: CFP China is willing to work with Australia to focus on common interests and boost cooperation in areas including green development and artificial intelligence (AI), Chinese Premier Li Qiang said during the 11th China-Australia Annual Leaders' Meeting with Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese in Beijing on Friday, according to the Xinhua News Agency. Noting next year marks the 55th anniversary of China-Australia diplomatic relations, Li said China stands ready to work with Australia to seize this opportunity to focus on common interests, properly manage differences, and deliver more outcomes in the comprehensive strategic partnership, Xinhua reported. China is willing to expand trade volume and optimize its structure with Australia, develop cooperation highlights in emerging areas such as green and low-carbon development, new energy vehicles and AI, and further enhance trade and investment liberalization and facilitation, Li said, per Xinhua. Albanese said Australia is willing to deepen cooperation with China in economy and trade, agriculture, energy and other fields, and accelerate cooperation in emerging fields like clean energy, AI, electric vehicles and digital economy, Xinhua reported. The leaders' calls for broader economic cooperation coincided with the ninth Australia-China CEO Roundtable, where Albanese and senior business executives gathered in Beijing on Friday to explore opportunities in resources, industrial decarbonization and clean energy. Mining cooperation, in particular, is expanding beyond traditional iron ore trade to green mining, renewable energy and low-carbon steelmaking. Co-hosted by the Business Council of Australia and China Development Bank, the meeting brought together 11 Australian executives, including representatives from BHP and Rio Tinto, alongside Chinese business leaders, according to Investing.com. China accounts for more than a quarter of Australia's international trade, according to the Business Council of Australia. Australia has long been a major iron ore supplier to China, while China is a major market for Australian resources. Australian miners account for nearly 60 percent of China's iron ore imports, while China produces more than half of the world's steel, according to Albanese's remarks at a bilateral steel decarbonization roundtable in July 2025. As the industry faces pressure to cut emissions, the two countries' complementary strengths are creating opportunities across the industrial chain, Chinese industry observers said. During a meeting between the Chinese and Australian leaders in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province, on Friday, the Chinese side called for deepening mutually beneficial cooperation in pursuit of the two countries' respective development goals, advancing traditional cooperation in areas such as energy and minerals, according to the Xinhua News Agency. Mark Kouwenhoven, general manager of Fortescue's China operations, told the Global Times that the company has operated large-scale mines in Australia's remote Pilbara region for more than two decades and is bringing together its mining experience and the capabilities of Chinese firms. "Our Chinese partners bring expertise in manufacturing, energy and technology. We are combining these strengths to demonstrate how decarbonization can be achieved at industrial scale," Kouwenhoven said. He cited cooperation with XCMG on all-electric mining equipment and partnerships with LONGi, BYD and Envision Energy in solar power, storage and wind power. Fortescue is integrating these technologies through a green power grid in the Pilbara and the electrification of its mining fleet, he said. Cooperation is also reaching further down the steelmaking chain. Rio Tinto, the University of Queensland, Central South University and the University of Science and Technology Liaoning recently established the Global Ironmaking Frontier Technical R&D Platform to advance low-carbon ironmaking research through joint work by Chinese and Australian researchers, according to the Australian company. Rio Tinto has also worked with China's Shougang Group on emissions-reduction technology. In September 2026, the two companies commissioned a carbon capture trial facility at Shougang's Jingtang base in Hebei Province, capable of processing up to 3,000 cubic meters of blast furnace gas per hour and capturing up to 10,000 tons of carbon dioxide annually, Rio Tinto said. The project builds on a 2022 partnership covering carbon capture and low-carbon steelmaking. Policy cooperation is developing alongside these projects. At the first Australia-China Policy Dialogue on Steel Decarbonisation on November 2, officials discussed iron ore processing, lower-emission steel technologies, industry standards and emissions accounting. The two sides agreed to continue exchanges and develop practical cooperation, with China set to host the next dialogue. Wang Guoqing, research director at Beijing Lange Steel Information Research Center, told the Global Times that the shift from iron ore trade toward green mining, low-carbon metallurgy and joint research is an inevitable trend amid global steel decarbonization and industrial upgrading. It does not replace existing trade but deepens the complementary relationship between the two countries. "Australia's strengths include high-grade iron ore, mature mining and mineral-processing expertise, abundant wind and solar resources, and research into low-carbon metallurgy and the utilization of lower-grade ore. China, meanwhile, has strengths in renewable energy equipment, mining machinery, autonomous mining trucks, smart mines and integrated energy systems, as well as experience applying low-carbon technologies across its large steel industry," Wang said. The two countries need to coordinate efforts to cut emissions across the entire chain, from mining and transportation to smelting, Wang said. This means integrating renewable power, energy storage and smart equipment at mining sites; establishing carbon-footprint tracking for ore transportation; and jointly developing hydrogen-based shaft furnaces and shorter-process steelmaking technologies suited to Australian iron ore, with green hydrogen metallurgy advancing in stages. As a major resource supplier and the world's largest steelmaking market, respectively, Australia and China could develop a more integrated low-carbon steel supply chain, Wang said. If translated into commercially viable projects, this cooperation could offer a practical model for the global mining and steel industries' green transition.

item.title: GT on the spot: From AI remixes to tea livestreams, young people bring fresh energy to ethnic unity in Yunnan
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20 21:04:00
Visitors experience the relaxed pace of life in Nuogan village on Jingmai Mountain in Pu'er, Southwest China's Yunnan Province. Photo: Li Hao/Global Times A Jingpo melody from Southwest China's Yunnan Province has found a new life on phone screens. Reworked with artificial intelligence and paired with striking dance videos, it has encouraged people far beyond its birthplace to follow the rhythm and discover the culture behind it. On Jingmai Mountain in Pu'er, another screen connects viewers with a different tradition. Xianjin, an ethnic Dai woman born in the 2000s, uses livestreams to talk about her hometown's tea, ancient forests and village life. During a recent reporting tour in Yunnan, Global Times reporter explored how younger generations are creating opportunities for exchange among ethnic groups, bringing fresh energy to efforts to forge a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation. Lyrics of the soil At Longchuan's Munao Zongge square in Dehong Dai and Jingpo Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan, local dancers in ethnic dress and visitors form long lines, moving to the same beat. The procession brings people together in an activity they can join without being professional performers or belonging to a particular ethnic group. The viral music has deep roots, but its present form is a recent creation. Jingpo artist Shi Legan composed the "Munao Zongge March" in 1991. Earlier this year, Beijing musician Zhen Zhen adapted that melody with new lyrics and AI-assisted arrangements and vocals. Without A-list celebrities or professional promotional campaigns, the song "Munao Zongge" has garnered nearly 3 billion views on China's major short-video platform Douyin. Munao Zongge, a major Jingpo celebration featuring collective dancing, was included in China's national intangible cultural heritage list in 2006. Its winding dance formations carry memories of the Jingpo people's migration, giving today's online enthusiasm a connection to a much longer history. The name carries the idea of gathering to sing and dance. During major celebrations, participants from neighboring ethnic groups also share a meal served on banana leaves, extending the gathering from the dance ground to the dining table. For Zhen, a video of mass dancing prompted an interest that became three weeks of work. Research changed his understanding of the music: early attempts to treat it as a love song gave way to lyrics informed by Jingpo history. AI helped him arrange the music and produce virtual voices, but its research results sometimes conflicted. He went back to books and papers to check the information himself. "Lyrics have to grow out of the soil," Zhen said. In Longchuan, community dance leader Song Haihe introduced that participants include locals from different ethnic groups alongside visitors from across the country. The cultural interest also brings visitors to local businesses. Longchuan received 42,000 domestic tourist visits during this year's National Day holiday, while overnight stays in commercial accommodation rose 11.07 percent year-on-year, according to the county's culture and tourism authorities. For someone first drawn to the music through a short video, these regular gatherings provide a place to learn its steps alongside local people. The encounter can continue after the video ends. Xianjin welcomes visitors to her family's tea shop in Nuogan village. Photo: Li Hao/Global Times Connections over tea On Jingmai Mountain, Xianjin faces a related task: giving people who discover her hometown online a reason to understand it more closely. An encounter at a tea exhibition in 2020 exposed a problem she would have to overcome. When she introduced tea from her hometown, a trader asked: "Where is Jingmai Mountain?" Having a distinctive product did not guarantee that buyers knew its origins. After returning home, she began livestreaming to introduce the tea and its place of origin. Her days combine brewing tea, making tea-flavored ice cream and filming village life. She opened a tea house after seeing more visitors arrive following the mountain's World Heritage inscription in 2023. Early in her business, she realized that selling the name "Jingmai tea" was insufficient. Her videos began showing what distinguished its place of origin: clouds over the mountain, hand-processing techniques and daily life in traditional houses. The landscape behind those sales is itself a product of longstanding cooperation. UNESCO describes Jingmai Mountain's tea-growing system as having developed over more than a thousand years through the practices of the Blang and Dai peoples. Tea grows beneath a forest canopy, within a landscape of villages, groves and protective forests. Local authorities told the Global Times that the inscribed heritage area includes five old tea forests, nine traditional villages and three protective partition forests. Protecting the trees also means maintaining the communities and knowledge that have sustained them. During the reporting tour, Xianjin pointed to renovated old houses and explained that residents of different ethnic groups had worked to preserve them. The forests and village buildings were a shared inheritance. Jingmai village official Yan Sailuan described cooperation that extends from celebrations to farm work. People gather in one another's villages for festivals, contribute labor and organize long-table banquets; during tea picking and other agricultural work, neighbors help one another. Skills circulate through the same relationships. In Wengji village, tea-processing heritage practitioner Sanwen teaches learners from different villages and ethnic groups. His workshop has also become a place where visitors can experience traditional tea making. The opportunities extend beyond individual businesses. Jingmai Mountain received 694,300 tourist visits in 2025, with culture and tourism revenue reaching 563 million yuan ($84.45 million). Residents have converted traditional homes into tea shops, restaurants and guesthouses, retaining the buildings' distinctive appearance while finding new uses for them. The younger generation is adding new partners to these networks. Xia Haoling, who previously worked in branding and new media in Shanghai, settled on Jingmai Mountain and established the Zhishan brand, developing scented sachets and incense inspired by local plants and Blang culture. The growing business has changed everyday logistics, too. Previously, tea sold online had to be packed late into the night and taken down to the township for dispatch the next morning. Couriers now come up to the village regularly to collect parcels. For Xianjin, the ancient forests remain the starting point of these new ventures. "These roots belong to all of us, whichever ethnic group we come from," she said.

item.title: Chinese boys, aged 14 and 3, set BMX and cartwheel records for Guinness World Records Day
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20 17:28:00
Liu Haoran November 19 marked the 22nd annual Guinness World Records Day. Challengers from around the world pushed the limits of human capability once again on the same day. Among them, two challengers from China attracted considerable attention: a 14-year-old who performed 10 consecutive flips in the air while riding a BMX bike, and a 3-year-old who performed 55 cartwheels in one minute on the ground. In China, 14-year-old BMX freestyle rider Liu Haoran set two records during this year's Guinness World Records Day challenge: "Most consecutive BMX side somersaults" (10 consecutive flips) and "Highest BMX backflip" (3.13 meters). Liu also improved on his own previous world record. A BMX backflip is a freestyle trick in which the rider and bike rotate 360 degrees backward mid-air off a ramp or jump before landing on the wheels. The flair is a highly difficult maneuver in BMX freestyle. Riders must launch themselves into the air on a ramp, simultaneously flipping themselves and their bikes sideways before landing precisely back down the ramp. Peng Yizhou The other challenger from China, Peng Yizhou, 3, a martial arts school student, completed 55 sidecar flips in one minute during this year's challenge, setting a Guinness World Record for the most cartwheels in one minute in the under 16 category. Peng was born in Tangyin County, Anyang City, Central China's Henan Province. His parents are both martial arts instructors. From the age of 7 months, Peng lived with his parents at a martial arts school, watching the older students practice martial arts. At the age of 2, he began to imitate cartwheels on his own and gradually learned to perform the movement independently under his father's guidance. In addition to cartwheels, he also enjoys swimming, playing with toys, and participating in activities with the older students at the martial arts school. For Peng, the cartwheel wasn't initially a competitive skill he needed to master; rather, it stemmed from curiosity and imitation of his surroundings. His parents recalled that when Peng first completed a cartwheel independently, he tried repeatedly, falling several times, until finally landing steadily and excitedly turning to his father, shouting, "Dad, I stood up!" item.title: Time for Takaichi to retract her erroneous 'survival-threatening situation' remarks
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20 12:35:00
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi speaks to reporters ahead of her departure for a tour of Europe at the Prime Minister's Official Residence in Tokyo on June 13, 2026. Photo: VCG On November 19, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi held a press conference after attending the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, reiterating that Japan's basic position on the Taiwan question remains consistent with the 1972 Sino-Japanese Joint Statement and emphasizing that "there has been absolutely no change to this position." She also said that "China is an important neighboring country," that the status of the four political documents as the "basic documents on Japan-China relations" remains unchanged, and that Japan is willing to comprehensively advance a strategic relationship of mutual benefit through dialogue and build "constructive and stable" China-Japan relations. However, when asked about with her erroneous remarks a year earlier that the Chinese mainland's "use of force on Taiwan" could constitute a "survival-threatening situation" for Japan, Takaichi continued to evade the question, saying that "she could not comment on hypothetical scenarios." The core principles of the Sino-Japanese Joint Statement are clearly set out in black and white: The Government of Japan recognizes that the Government of the People's Republic of China as the sole legal Government of China. The Government of the People's Republic of China reiterates that Taiwan is an inalienable part of the territory of the People's Republic of China. The Government of Japan fully understands and respects this stand of the Government of the People's Republic of China, and it firmly maintains its stand under Article 8 of the Postdam Proclamation. This statement, together with the other four political documents, including the Treaty of Peace and Friendship between China and Japan, forms the political foundation for the normalization of diplomatic relations between the two countries. These are commitments that both countries must uphold in their bilateral relations and an important part of the postwar international order. Linking a "contingency in Taiwan" to a "survival-threatening situation" for Japan and implying that Japan might exercise its right to collective self-defense directly undermines the framework established by the 1972 Sino-Japanese Joint Statement and seriously deviates from the postwar international order that Japan, as a defeated nation in World War II, is obliged to observe. If Japan's position on the Taiwan question is truly consistent with the Sino-Japan Joint Statement, it should acknowledge its mistake and publicly retract the provocative claim that "a Taiwan contingency is a Japan contingency." On the same day, the leaders of China, Russia and the US held a historic trilateral meeting in Shenzhen and issued the China-Russia-US Heads of State Declaration toward Peace. All three leaders recalled the history of their countries fighting side by side during World War II, sending an important signal of their shared commitment to safeguarding the postwar international order - a message that Tokyo should take note of. The core documents underpinning the postwar international order include the Cairo Declaration and the Potsdam Proclamation, which made clear that Japan must return the Chinese territories it had seized, including Taiwan. Japan accepted the Potsdam Proclamation and surrendered unconditionally, and subsequently reaffirmed its commitment to adhering to Article 8 of the proclamation in the Sino-Japan Joint Statement. Any remarks that directly link the Taiwan question to Japan's security, or even imply possible military intervention, constitute an open challenge to the outcomes of the victory in World War II and the postwar international order. China-Japan relations remain strained over remarks concerning Taiwan, with tensions already affecting economic and trade ties, people-to-people exchanges and other areas. Takaichi has emphasized dialogue and a strategic relationship of mutual benefit, but her words must be matched by actions. If she sincerely wishes to improve China-Japan relations, retracting her erroneous remarks should be the first step. Otherwise, merely repeating that Japan's "position remains unchanged" without making substantive corrections will do little to inspire confidence or benefit Japan itself, or contribute to lasting peace and stability in the region.
